narrative.overview: The look comes straight from the Agents for Change artwork: a charcoal ground, chalk-white type, and rounded-square tiles in lime, pink and chalk with a shape cut out so the ground shows through. The tiles turn a quarter when you reach for them. Everything else is quiet: a clean neo-grotesque, dark panels to work in, and one light page at the end, the record, so it prints.
keyCharacteristics: Three tile shapes from the artwork (bite, gear, molecule), drawn from its own paths, at quarter-turns.
Inter Tight for the name and headings, Inter for reading.
Lime is what you press and what is chosen. Pink is people and their words, and the soft alerts.
Corners are a quarter of the height, like the tiles.

rules.name: The One Lime Button Rule
rules.body: Each view has one lime button that matters most. Others are chalk outlines.

rules.name: The Lime Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what you press, what's current or what's picked. It never decorates something the person hasn't reached.

rules.name: The Pink Is People Rule
rules.body: Pink carries other people's words and gentle warnings. It is never something you press.

rules.name: The Emphasis Is Lime Rule
rules.body: Headline emphasis is the same face in lime. No italics, highlighter strokes or gradient text.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small labels above headings. A heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Board Stays Flat Rule
rules.body: Group entries on the board have no box or shadow. Only working panels lift.

dos: Do keep one lime button per view.
Do use lime only for what is pressed, chosen or current.
Do put people's words in pink.
Do keep corners at a quarter of the height.
Do give a new group its three tiles in ORG_TILES.
donts: Don't use pink for buttons, links or anything you press.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't put a box or shadow round board entries.
Don't invent new tile shapes; use the artwork's three.
Don't use sparkles, glows, gradient text or any "magic" AI imagery.
